reference_sql:
SELECT p.product_id, COALESCE(SUM(s.units), 0) AS first_week_units
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN sales s
  ON s.product_id = p.product_id
 AND s.order_date >= p.launch_date
 AND s.order_date < p.launch_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY
WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id
alternatives:
WITH first_week AS (  -- one row per product that sold in its first 7 days
  SELECT s.product_id, SUM(s.units) AS units
  FROM sales s
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = s.product_id
  WHERE s.order_date BETWEEN p.launch_date AND p.launch_date + 6
  GROUP BY s.product_id
)
SELECT p.product_id, COALESCE(f.units, 0) AS first_week_units
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN first_week f ON f.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'

SELECT p.product_id, COALESCE(SUM(s.units) FILTER (WHERE s.order_date >= p.launch_date AND s.order_date < p.launch_date + INTERVAL 7 DAY), 0) AS first_week_units FROM products p LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' GROUP BY p.product_id

other_way.sql:
WITH first_week AS (  -- one row per product that sold in its first 7 days
  SELECT s.product_id, SUM(s.units) AS units
  FROM sales s
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = s.product_id
  WHERE s.order_date BETWEEN p.launch_date AND p.launch_date + 6
  GROUP BY s.product_id
)
SELECT p.product_id, COALESCE(f.units, 0) AS first_week_units
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN first_week f ON f.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
other_way.tradeoff: Adding up the first week in its own step keeps the join simple, but the window in the LEFT JOIN's ON does it in one pass.

solver.query:
SELECT p.product_id, COALESCE(SUM(s.units), 0) AS first_week_units
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
  AND CAST(s.order_date AS DATE) BETWEEN CAST(p.launch_date AS DATE) AND CAST(p.launch_date AS DATE) + 6
WHERE CAST(p.launch_date AS DATE) >= DATE '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id
